facebook.long_form:
The road to LA28 is official.

With Group Oklahoma now complete — USA going 5-0, advancing alongside Mexico as direct qualifiers, and China locking up the Wild Card — the eight-nation field for the 2027 WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Finals is set.

The April 5–11 Redcliffe bracket: USA | Mexico | China | Australia | Canada | Japan | Puerto Rico | Chinese Taipei

Talobilla Park, 45 minutes from Brisbane, will host the game that matters most: a World Championship title and an LA28 Olympic qualification spot on the line.

For USA, the work is already underway. Patty Gasso — who coaches the Sooners at Oklahoma AND serves as WNT head coach — now faces the challenge of keeping her roster sharp through two different calendars. Olivia Brady's 3-home-run Group Oklahoma performance announced her as a genuine international power threat. And the veterans — Garcia and Mulipola among them — bring Olympic and World Games pedigree to every at-bat.

Eight nations. One April window. The path to LA28 starts now.
facebook.image_caption: Eight nations confirmed. One title up for grabs in Redcliffe, QLD (April 5–11, 2027). The road to LA28 is set — and USA is ready. #SoftballUSA

stories.title: Oklahoma Sooners — Day 5 Full-Staff Fall Camp, 9 Days to Opener
stories.angle: The Wells-Berzon-Harter trio takes shape as the opener approaches.

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
OU softball enters Day 5 of full-staff fall camp with 9 days to its Sept. 30 opener vs. Tarleton State.

Kendall Wells (32 HR, NCAA freshman record). Sydney Berzon (2x All-American, 406 career K). Macie Harter (.346). This roster is loaded. #Sooners

facebook.long_form:
Oklahoma softball is 9 days from its Sept. 30 opener, and Patty Gasso's rebuilt roster is taking shape at Love's Field.

Day 5 of full-staff fall camp features three of the most anticipated names in the country working together in practice: Kendall Wells — the 2026 NFCA Freshman of Year who broke the NCAA single-season freshman home run record with 32 — Sydney Berzon, the 2x All-American transfer from LSU (486.1 IP career, 2.02 ERA, 406 strikeouts), and Macie Harter (.346 BA at Middle Tennessee State), who brings contact and gap-to-gap pop to a lineup that needs both.

12 returners. 9 newcomers. A fall schedule that runs from Sept. 30 (Tarleton State) through Nov. 4 (East Texas A&M). The Sooners are building under the brightest spotlight in softball — and practice is where it all starts.

All eight fall games at Love's Field. General admission: $10.88 per game. All Fall Pass: $70.69.
facebook.image_caption: Day 5. Nine days to go. Oklahoma's new-look lineup is finding its identity — and the clock is ticking toward the Sept. 30 opener. #Sooners

stories.title: Class of 2028 — Landers to Texas, Schlader to OU; Big Week Reshapes the Class
stories.angle: Two program-defining commits in one week — Texas got the No. 1 MIF, OU got the No. 1 pitcher.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
BREAKING: Michaela Landers — No. 1 overall prospect in the 2028 class (Softball America) — has committed to Texas.

The Waxahachie, TX native hit .639 with 25 HR and 52 extra-base hits this year. She's a Longhorn. #HookEm

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Oklahoma answers: No. 1-ranked pitcher Sophia Schlader commits to OU.

The Iowa Gatorade Player of Year went 30-1 with 296 K in 187 IP as a sophomore. She's a Sooner — and she chose OU over Texas. #Sooners

facebook.long_form:
The biggest week of the 2028 recruiting class just happened — and two rival programs are walking away with franchise-level commitments.

Michaela Landers → Texas: The No. 1 overall prospect in the 2028 class (Softball America) committed to the Longhorns on Sept. 18. The Waxahachie, TX native is a five-tool shortstop/MIF who hit .639 with 25 HR (Dallas-area record), 73 runs and 52 extra-base hits in 41 games. She chose Texas over Oklahoma and Florida.

Sophia Schlader → Oklahoma: Days later, OU landed the No. 1-ranked pitcher and No. 3 overall player in the class: Sophia Schlader from Waukee Northwest HS in Iowa. The 2025-26 Iowa Gatorade Player of Year is a two-time state champion who went 30-1 with 296 strikeouts in 187 innings as a sophomore. She chose OU over Texas.

The scoreboard after Day 13 of the in-person window: Williams (OU) | Landers (Texas) | Donalson (FSU) | Saenz (OU) | Schlader (OU) | Gutierrez (TTU) | Galindo + Wilson (Tennessee) | Losh + Harris (Florida) | Myers (South Carolina) | Ridling + Stell (Arizona) | Eldred (Tennessee)

1,226 Extra Innings nominations — an all-time class record. Top uncommitted: Holden, Bennett.
facebook.image_caption: No. 1 bat to Texas. No. 1 arm to Oklahoma. In one extraordinary week, the 2028 recruiting class found its two defining stories. #Softball2028

stories.title: Texas Longhorns — Landers Commit + 8 Days to Sept. 29 Opener
stories.angle: Landers to Texas adds fuel to the three-peat fire — the program's pipeline now spans from Kavan's senior season through a top-5 2028 class.

x_posts.label: Post 6
x_posts.text:
Texas lands the No. 1 overall 2028 recruit. The fall opener is 8 days away. Isa Torres and Jordy Kavan are ready.

The Longhorns don't just play for this season. They're building something. Sept. 29 vs. Murray State — free. #HookEm

facebook.long_form:
Eight days. That's how long Texas has before its fall season opener — and the program has never looked more complete.

The reigning national champions (53-12, 2026 WCWS title) return with Isa Torres (2026 D1Softball Player of Year, .530 BA, 16 HR, 56 RBI from FSU, Georgetown TX native), Jordy Kavan (2x WCWS MOP — the only player in history to win it twice), and Karen White (NFCA Staff of Year, 2nd consecutive). And now: Michaela Landers — No. 1 overall 2028 recruit — is a Longhorn.

Sept. 29 vs. Murray State. McCombs Field. 6 PM CT. Free admission.

A three-peat would put Texas alongside UCLA (1988–90) and Oklahoma (2021–23) as the only programs in history to win three consecutive national titles. The Longhorns don't just play for this season — they're building something bigger.
facebook.image_caption: Landers committed. Torres ready. Kavan enters her final season. Texas opens fall ball Sept. 29 — and the three-peat chase is officially on. #HookEm

stories.title: Texas Tech — Glasco Year 2, Week 3 Execution Mode
stories.angle: Seven All-Americans, one shared hunger — TTU enters the back third of fall with chemistry crystallizing.

x_posts.label: Post 7
x_posts.text:
Texas Tech's 7 All-Americans enter Week 3 of fall ball together — the most in any fall roster in program history.

Beachum. Pickering. Heavener. And four more. Glasco's Year 2 project is turning from chemistry to identity. #WreckEm

facebook.long_form:
No program in Texas Tech softball history has assembled what Gerry Glasco has in Lubbock right now: seven All-Americans on one fall roster, practicing together entering Week 3.

Jaysoni Beachum — .406 BA, 10 HR, 69 RBI, All-ACC 1st Team at Florida State.
Kasidi Pickering — .384 career BA, 50 HR at Oklahoma, the No. 2 transfer in the portal.
Jayden Heavener — 13-9, 2.81 ERA, 128 K as a lefty at LSU.
Plus four more.

Gerry Glasco — Big 12 Coach of Year in both 2025 and 2026 — knows what it takes to build a winner in Lubbock. The 2026 season ended as WCWS runner-up at 61-10. Year 2 is about finishing.

Week 3 is where chemistry becomes identity. Where practice reps turn into game reads. Where Glasco finds out if this collection of talent can become a team that wins it all.
facebook.image_caption: Seven All-Americans. Week 3. Texas Tech's fall ball experiment is becoming something real — and Glasco's Year 2 mission is crystal clear: finish what 2026 started. #WreckEm
